title: AI Unlocked: Politics & Governance
blurb: For campaigners, public servants, and civic organizations: policy analysis at speed, constituent communication, campaign operations, disinformation defense, and the ethics/regulation landscape shaping AI in public life.

modules.t: AI in Public Life: The Map
modules.d: How AI is entering government, parliaments, campaigns and civil society — and the democratic values at stake.
modules.body:
Why public life is different

When businesses adopt AI, the main stakes are efficiency and competitiveness. In public life, the stakes include rights, trust and democratic legitimacy. A government chatbot that gives wrong benefit information, an algorithm that unfairly flags citizens for investigation, or a deepfake released days before an election can harm individuals and erode trust in institutions. Public servants, elected officials, campaigners and civic organisations therefore carry special responsibilities when using AI.

The landscape

  • Government and public administration: drafting documents, summarising consultations, answering citizen enquiries, translating services, analysing data for planning, fraud detection and case management.
  • Parliaments and legislatures: summarising bills and amendments, comparing laws across jurisdictions, analysing public submissions and supporting committee research.
  • Political campaigns and parties: message drafting, voter outreach, volunteer coordination, fundraising communications and opposition research.
  • Civil society and advocacy: policy analysis, campaign materials, monitoring of government performance and elections, and fact-checking.
  • Media and information ecosystems: AI-generated content, recommendation algorithms and synthetic media that shape what citizens see.

Democratic values as a lens

Evaluate any AI use in public life against core democratic values: legality (lawful authority and compliance), accountability (identifiable humans answerable for decisions), transparency (people know when and how AI is used in decisions affecting them), equality and non-discrimination, privacy, participation (citizens can be heard and contest decisions), and truthfulness in public communication. The OECD AI Principles and UNESCO's Recommendation on the Ethics of AI articulate similar values internationally.

Cautionary cases. In the Netherlands, a childcare benefits scandal involving risk-scoring and discriminatory practices wrongly accused thousands of families of fraud, contributing to the government's resignation in 2021. In Australia, the automated "Robodebt" debt-recovery scheme was found unlawful and the subject of a Royal Commission in 2023. Both show how automated decision-making without legality, fairness and human accountability can cause serious harm to citizens.

Regulation is developing

The European Union's AI Act classifies several public-sector uses — such as access to essential public services and benefits, law enforcement and migration — and AI systems intended to influence elections or voting behaviour, as high-risk, with obligations for risk management, transparency and human oversight. The EU has also adopted rules on the transparency and targeting of political advertising. Many countries are developing national AI strategies and laws, and data protection laws apply widely, including across Africa. Political actors must know the rules in every jurisdiction where they operate.

Neutrality of this course

This course is non-partisan. Its methods apply equally to governments and oppositions, parties of any orientation, and civic organisations of any cause. The common standard is lawful, truthful, accountable and fair use of AI in public life.

🧪 Interactive Lab — try it now

Act as my public-sector AI advisor. Ask me whether I work in government, a legislature, a campaign or civil society, and my country. Map the AI uses relevant to my role, evaluate each against legality, accountability, transparency, equality, privacy, participation and truthfulness, and identify which uses would likely be high-risk under frameworks such as the EU AI Act. Remind me to verify the current laws in my jurisdiction.

📚 Glossary

  • Automated decision-making: decisions made by systems with little or no human involvement
  • High-risk AI: EU AI Act category requiring strict obligations
  • Democratic legitimacy: public acceptance that authority is exercised rightfully
  • Synthetic media: AI-generated or manipulated audio, images or video

📖 References

  • OECD (2019, updated 2024). Recommendation of the Council on Artificial Intelligence.
  • UNESCO (2021). Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence.
  • European Union — Artificial Intelligence Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689), Annex III.
  • Royal Commission into the Robodebt Scheme (Australia, 2023), Final Report.
  • Dutch Parliamentary Inquiry into the childcare benefits affair (2020).

quiz.q: A social-affairs ministry in Yaounde plans an algorithm that flags benefit recipients as likely fraudsters and suspends payments automatically pending review. The vendor reports 94% accuracy. What should the ministry's adviser insist on first?
opts: Pilot it in one region first and suspend payments just where the risk score exceeds a high threshold
Launch with the 94% model but publish the accuracy figure so citizens understand the error rate
A clear legal basis, bias testing across groups, a named accountable official and a way to contest flags
Keep the scoring criteria confidential so fraudsters cannot learn to game the risk model
quiz.x: Robodebt and the Dutch childcare scandal show that legality, fairness testing, human accountability and contestability come first. A regional pilot with a threshold is the runner-up but still suspends payments automatically without those safeguards.

quiz.q: An EU member-state agency is buying an AI system that helps decide who receives emergency housing support. Under the EU AI Act, how is this system most likely classified?
opts: Minimal-risk, since a trained caseworker signs the final decision on each file
High-risk, because it affects access to essential public services and benefits
Limited-risk, needing just a notice that users are interacting with AI
Prohibited, because public bodies may not use AI to allocate welfare
quiz.x: Annex III lists access to essential public services and benefits as high-risk, bringing risk-management, transparency and oversight duties. Having a caseworker sign off does not move it to minimal-risk, and such uses are regulated rather than banned.

quiz.q: A parliamentary research unit in Accra uses AI to summarise 3,000 public submissions on a land bill. Which democratic value is most at stake if the summary quietly drops minority viewpoints?
opts: Participation, because citizens' contributions must genuinely be heard
Legality, because the bill's enabling statute requires the consultation
Truthfulness, because the summary is published as a public document
Privacy, because submissions may contain names and village locations
quiz.x: Participation means citizens can be heard and influence decisions; a summary that erases minority views undermines that directly. Truthfulness is a defensible runner-up, but the core harm is to people's voice in the process.

quiz.q: A city council in Ohio uses an AI chatbot to answer property-tax questions. Residents are not told it is automated, and its answers are not logged. Which two values from the module are most directly weakened?
opts: Truthfulness and equality
Legality and data privacy
Equality and participation in decisions
Transparency and accountability
quiz.x: Not disclosing automation undermines transparency; no logs mean no identifiable human can review and answer for errors, which weakens accountability. Truthfulness may be affected later, but the described design flaws are about disclosure and answerability.

quiz.q: A civil-society group in Douala asks its trainer whether this course will help it criticise the governing party's use of AI. How should the trainer describe the course's stance?
opts: It takes no position on standards and leaves ethics to each organisation
It focuses on government users, since they hold the most public power
It mainly equips opposition parties and civic groups to hold incumbents to account
It applies the same lawful, truthful and fair standard to every actor and cause
quiz.x: The course is explicitly non-partisan: the same standard of lawful, truthful, accountable, fair use applies to governments, oppositions and civic groups alike. Focusing on government is tempting but is not the stated scope.

quiz.q: A Kenyan county government wants to rank villages for borehole investment using an AI model trained on past spending data. Past spending favoured well-connected areas. What is the main risk?
opts: The model may be too slow to process data for all 300 villages in one budget cycle
Engineers may struggle to explain the ranking method to the county assembly
The model may reproduce historic inequities and breach equality and non-discrimination
Using any spending data at all could breach data protection rules on public records
quiz.x: Training on biased past allocations can encode the same favouritism, a core equality concern. Explainability to the assembly matters too, but it is secondary to the risk of systematically unfair outcomes.

quiz.q: A ministry's communications team posts an AI-generated infographic with a literacy statistic that no official source contains. A journalist asks where it came from. Which value was breached and what is the right response?
opts: Privacy; remove the graphic and review what data was used to produce it
Truthfulness; correct it promptly and visibly with the verified figure
Legality; seek legal advice before acknowledging any error publicly
Participation; invite the public to comment on which figure is accurate
quiz.x: Publishing a fabricated figure breaches truthfulness in public communication, and corrections should be prompt and visible. Seeking legal advice first delays a correction the public is owed.

quiz.q: A government in West Africa asks which international instruments set out values similar to the course's democratic lens for public-sector AI. Which pair fits best?
opts: The OECD AI Principles and UNESCO's Recommendation on the Ethics of AI
The Paris Agreement and the Sustainable Development Goal on education
The Budapest Convention on Cybercrime and the UN Charter's Article 2
The Basel III accords and the Malabo Convention on cyber security
quiz.x: The lesson names the OECD AI Principles and UNESCO's Recommendation as articulating similar values. The Malabo Convention is a real African data and cyber instrument but is not the one cited for AI ethics values, and Basel III is about banking.

quiz.q: A US state election office pilots an AI tool that predicts which registered voters have moved, to send them removal notices. Which statement best describes the risk level and what is needed?
opts: Low risk provided the vendor is US-based and certified for election equipment
Significant risk to rights; it needs accuracy testing, human review and appeal routes
Low risk, since a mailed notice gives voters a chance to respond and correct it
Moderate risk that largely disappears if the predictions are published in aggregate form
quiz.x: Wrongly removing voters affects a fundamental right, so it needs testing, human review and contestability. A mailed notice is a partial safeguard, but people often miss mail and errors can still disenfranchise them.

quiz.q: Before a training session, a Cameroonian deputy's aide says: 'AI is just a productivity tool; the stakes are the same as in a business.' What is the best rebuttal from this module?
opts: In public life the stakes include rights, trust and democratic legitimacy
Public bodies have smaller budgets, so mistakes are costlier to fix than in firms
Public bodies face stricter procurement law, which slows any AI adoption
Businesses are regulated by the EU AI Act, while public bodies largely are not
quiz.x: The module's opening point is that public-sector AI affects rights, trust and legitimacy, not just efficiency. Procurement constraints are real but are not why the stakes differ, and the AI Act covers public uses heavily.

facts.t: Year the Dutch government resigned over the childcare benefits scandal.
facts.more: Risk-scoring and discriminatory practices wrongly accused thousands of families of fraud. Automated suspicion without legality and human accountability became a national political crisis.

facts.t: Australia's automated debt-recovery scheme, found unlawful and examined by a Royal Commission.
facts.more: The Royal Commission reported in 2023. Income averaging produced debts many citizens did not owe. Legality has to be checked before automation, not after the harm is done.

facts.t: The part of the EU AI Act that lists high-risk uses, including public services and elections.
facts.more: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 treats access to essential public benefits, law enforcement, migration and systems meant to influence voting as high-risk. These carry risk-management, transparency and human-oversight duties.

facts.t: UNESCO member states that adopted the Recommendation on the Ethics of AI in 2021.
facts.more: It is the first global standard on AI ethics. Together with the OECD AI Principles (2019, updated 2024), it gives public bodies anywhere, Cameroon included, a shared language for values.

labs.title: Which democratic value is most at stake?
labs.intro: Each case puts one value from the module's lens under strain. Put it in the bucket for the value most directly at risk.
items: A ministry starts auto-rejecting permit applications with no legal text authorising it
No named official can explain who approved a benefits algorithm
Citizens are not told that a chatbot pre-screened their complaint
Rejected applicants have no way to contest a risk score
A fraud model flags people with dual nationality far more often
A council shares a list of complainants' phone numbers with a vendor for 'training'
A municipality's AI summary of a consultation can't be published or checked
A tax-audit tool is in use before any legal basis is adopted
labs.tip: Several values often overlap. Ask which failure would hurt citizens first, and which one a court or auditor would point to.

labs.title: Actor and the AI use that fits its mandate
labs.intro: Match each public-life actor to the AI use that belongs to its role.
pairs: Answering citizen enquiries on renewing an ID card
Comparing an amendment against three earlier versions of a bill
Tracing the first upload of a viral video
Testing whether a benefits algorithm treats regions equally
labs.tip: The same tool serves different actors. What changes is the mandate, and with it the duties.

plaibox.title: Simulation: the fraud-scoring offer
plaibox.intro: You advise a regional social-services directorate in Bamenda. A vendor offers an AI tool to score benefit claimants for fraud risk. Scoring: 2 = best practice, 1 = partial, 0 = risky.

steps.s: The vendor says the tool is 'proven in Europe' and can go live next month.
o: Ask what legal basis lets the directorate score claimants at all
Legality comes first. Without lawful authority, nothing else about the tool matters.
Request the European accuracy figures before deciding
Useful, but accuracy elsewhere says nothing about legality or fairness in your context.
Accept a free trial on live claims to see how it performs
Live claims mean real citizens get scored by a tool with no legal basis or safeguards.

steps.s: The legal basis is confirmed. The model uses home district and language as inputs.
o: Keep them: they measurably improve prediction accuracy
Proxies like these can reproduce the discrimination seen in the Dutch scandal.
Test outcomes by district and language group before any use
Testing for disparate impact is the equality safeguard. Then you decide on the inputs with evidence.
Remove both inputs and proceed with the rollout
A reasonable instinct, but other variables can act as proxies. You still need to test outcomes.

steps.s: Staff propose that high scores trigger automatic suspension of payments.
o: Use scores only to prioritise human review, recording reasons
A human stays accountable, and citizens can be given reasons they can contest.
Suspend automatically, but allow appeals within 30 days
This is the Robodebt pattern: the harm lands first and the burden falls on citizens.
Suspend only for scores above 95%, where errors are rare
A higher threshold cuts errors but is still automated punishment with no human decision.

steps.s: A journalist asks how the directorate uses AI on claims.
o: Decline to comment, so fraudsters cannot game the model
Secrecy erodes trust and fails the transparency standard.
Publish a plain notice on purpose, safeguards and how to contest
This is transparency in practice and it passes the legitimacy test.
Confirm AI is used but give no details about how it works
Partly honest, but citizens still can't understand or challenge decisions.

plaibox.win: Strong judgement: legality, then fairness testing, then human accountability, then transparency. This is the order that protects citizens.
plaibox.lose: Revisit the democratic-values lens and the Dutch and Robodebt cases. Automation without lawful authority, testing and human decisions harms citizens.

modules.d: Using AI to research, compare and draft policy — with evidence, balance and verification.
modules.body:
The policy cycle

Public policy typically moves through agenda setting (defining the problem), formulation (developing options), decision (adoption by authorised bodies), implementation and evaluation. AI can accelerate research and drafting at each stage — but policy quality depends on evidence, stakeholder insight and judgement about values and trade-offs, which remain human responsibilities.

Problem definition and evidence

Strong policy begins with a precise problem statement supported by data: who is affected, how much, where and why. AI can help structure the problem, suggest causes and identify data sources, but statistics must come from verifiable sources such as national statistics institutes, administrative data, peer-reviewed research and reputable international organisations. Generative AI can fabricate statistics and citations; every figure in a policy paper must be traced to its source.

Comparative policy research

Policymakers often ask how other countries have addressed similar problems. AI can quickly outline approaches and point to examples, but laws, institutions and contexts differ. Verify each example in primary sources (official legislation, government reports, evaluations) and assess transferability: Does the context resemble yours in institutions, capacity, culture and resources? What evidence shows it worked, and for whom?

Options analysis. Good policy advice presents several realistic options — including doing nothing or improving existing measures — and assesses each against explicit criteria: effectiveness, cost, equity, feasibility, legal compliance, political acceptability and risks. AI can draft an options matrix from your inputs; you supply the evidence and weigh the trade-offs.

Regulatory impact assessment

Many governments use regulatory impact assessment (RIA) to analyse the expected benefits, costs and distributional effects of proposed rules before adoption, with consultation of affected parties. AI can help structure an RIA, summarise consultation responses and draft sections — while economists, legal experts and stakeholders provide the analysis and validation.

Legislative drafting and analysis

AI can summarise bills, compare versions and amendments, identify affected existing laws, translate between official languages, and draft explanatory notes in plain language. Legal drafting itself requires qualified legislative drafters: precision of terms, consistency with the constitution and existing law, enforceability, and the jurisdiction's drafting conventions. In bilingual systems such as Cameroon's (English and French), both language versions must be consistent and legally equivalent.

Balanced analysis

AI outputs can reflect biases in their training data and in how questions are framed. Ask for the strongest arguments for and against each option, the interests of different stakeholder groups, and evidence that challenges your preferred position. Analysts who serve the public have a duty to present evidence honestly, even when it is politically inconvenient.

Stakeholder mapping

Policies succeed or fail with stakeholders — citizens, businesses, civil society, implementing agencies, local authorities, unions and international partners. AI can draft stakeholder maps and anticipate concerns; genuine consultation, especially with affected and marginalised groups, cannot be simulated.

🧪 Interactive Lab — try it now

Act as my policy analyst. I will describe a policy problem and my country context. Help me write a precise problem statement, list the evidence I need and where to find it, outline approaches used elsewhere (marked for verification in primary sources), and build an options matrix including the status quo, assessed on effectiveness, cost, equity, feasibility, legal compliance, political acceptability and risk. Present the strongest arguments for and against each option.

📚 Glossary

  • Policy cycle: agenda setting, formulation, decision, implementation, evaluation
  • Regulatory impact assessment: analysis of a proposed regulation's benefits, costs and effects
  • Options matrix: comparison of policy options against explicit criteria
  • Transferability: whether a policy can work in a different context
  • Explanatory note: plain-language description of a bill's purpose and effects

📖 References

  • OECD — Regulatory Impact Assessment best practice principles.
  • Bardach, E. & Patashnik, E. A Practical Guide for Policy Analysis: The Eightfold Path to More Effective Problem Solving.
  • World Bank — Global Indicators of Regulatory Governance.
  • Cartwright, N. & Hardie, J. (2012). Evidence-Based Policy: A Practical Guide to Doing It Better.

quiz.q: A Ghanaian policy officer asks an AI tool for the national youth unemployment rate and gets '23.4%, Ghana Statistical Service 2022'. The figure will appear in a cabinet memo. What should she do?
opts: Round it to 'about one in four' so a small error would not change the message
Use it, since the AI named an official source, and add a footnote to that agency
Ask a second AI tool for the same figure and use it if the two answers match
Find the figure in the statistical service's own publication before using it
quiz.x: Generative AI can fabricate statistics and citations, so every figure must be traced to its source. Cross-checking with another AI is a tempting runner-up but both tools can share the same error.

quiz.q: A Rwandan ministry is drafting a plastic-bag policy and the AI suggests copying a Scandinavian deposit-return scheme. What is the key question before recommending it?
opts: Whether the Scandinavian scheme was popular with voters when it was introduced
Whether the AI tool cited the Scandinavian law correctly with an official gazette reference
Whether context matches in institutions and capacity, and evidence shows it worked
Whether the scheme is still in force and was adopted by a democratic parliament
quiz.x: Transferability depends on similar institutions, capacity, culture and resources plus evidence of effectiveness. Checking the gazette citation is necessary verification but does not tell you whether it would work in Rwanda.

quiz.q: An analyst in Abuja builds an options matrix for reducing road deaths: speed cameras, helmet enforcement and driver training. Her director says it is incomplete. What is most likely missing?
opts: A status quo or improve-existing-measures option on the same criteria
A separate AI-generated summary of public opinion on each option
A ranking of the options by which one the minister prefers
A list of the vendors who could supply speed cameras and training
quiz.x: Good options analysis includes doing nothing or improving existing measures, assessed against explicit criteria. Public opinion is one criterion (political acceptability), not a missing option.

quiz.q: A regulator in Nairobi has received 1,200 consultation responses on a new fintech rule as part of a regulatory impact assessment. What is the best role for AI here?
opts: Decide which responses are representative and drop the duplicates sent by organised campaigns
Replace the consultation step, since the AI has already seen sector data online
Summarise themes and draft sections, with economists and lawyers validating the analysis
Estimate the rule's costs and benefits directly, since it can model the sector
quiz.x: AI can structure an RIA and summarise consultation responses, while experts and stakeholders provide and validate the analysis. Filtering 'representative' responses is a judgement that should stay with humans.

quiz.q: Cameroon's legislature is preparing a bill in English and French. A clerk proposes using AI to translate the French text and publishing the result as the English version. What is the main issue?
opts: AI translations are not admissible as official parliamentary records in any country
Both versions must be legally equivalent, so qualified drafters must review the English
The English text should be drafted first, because common law is the senior tradition
Publication should wait until a third, neutral language version can be produced
quiz.x: In bilingual systems both versions must be consistent and legally equivalent, which requires qualified drafters. AI can assist translation; the claim that it is inadmissible everywhere is an overstatement.

quiz.q: A think tank in Washington asks an AI to 'write a brief showing why a soda tax works'. The resulting paper is one-sided. What prompt change best reflects the module's guidance?
opts: Ask for a shorter brief, since long briefs tend to amplify framing bias
Ask the AI to cite at least ten peer-reviewed studies to strengthen the brief's credibility
Ask for a neutral tone and remove adjectives that sound like advocacy
Ask for the strongest case for and against, stakeholder interests and contrary evidence
quiz.x: Balanced analysis requires asking for the strongest arguments on both sides, stakeholder interests and evidence against your preferred position. A neutral tone hides bias rather than correcting it, and AI-listed studies still need verification.

quiz.q: A district health team has a budget of 60 million FCFA. Option A reaches 12,000 people for 48 million; Option B reaches 9,000 people for 27 million. On cost per person reached, which is more efficient?
opts: Option A, because it reaches 3,000 more people
Option B, at about 3,000 FCFA per person
Option A, at about 4,000 FCFA per person
They are equal at roughly 3,500 FCFA per person
quiz.x: A costs 48m/12,000 = 4,000 FCFA per person; B costs 27m/9,000 = 3,000 FCFA. Reach favours A, but efficiency favours B; the options matrix should show both alongside equity and feasibility.

quiz.q: A ministry stakeholder map produced by AI lists farmers' unions, traders and NGOs with predicted concerns. The minister wants to skip field consultations to save time. What is the best advice?
opts: Use the map as preparation, but still consult affected and marginalised groups directly
Agree, since the AI map was built from many published sources on these groups
Ask the AI to simulate a consultation with each group and record the transcript
Run an online survey instead, which is faster and reaches more people than village meetings
quiz.x: AI can draft stakeholder maps, but genuine consultation, especially with marginalised groups, cannot be simulated. An online survey is a runner-up, yet it misses people without connectivity, often the most affected.

quiz.q: At which stage of the policy cycle is a ministry operating when it uses AI to compare reported school-meal outcomes against the targets set two years ago?
opts: Formulation
Agenda setting
Evaluation
Implementation
quiz.x: Comparing outcomes against targets after a programme has run is evaluation. Implementation is the runner-up, but that stage concerns delivering the programme, not assessing its results.

quiz.q: A senate staffer uses AI to compare two versions of an amendment and draft a plain-language explanatory note. Which task still requires a qualified legislative drafter?
opts: Producing a plain-language note for constituents about the amendment
Translating the explanatory note for a second official language audience
Listing which sections changed between the two versions of the text
Ensuring terms are precise, constitutional and consistent with existing law
quiz.x: Comparing versions and drafting notes are tasks AI can assist; precision, constitutional consistency and enforceability need a qualified drafter. Translation also needs review, but legal drafting itself is the protected task.

facts.t: The policy cycle: agenda setting, formulation, decision, implementation, evaluation.
facts.more: AI can speed up research and drafting at every stage. The judgements about evidence, values and trade-offs stay with people.

facts.t: Bardach's 'Eightfold Path' for practical policy analysis.
facts.more: Define the problem, assemble evidence, construct alternatives, select criteria, project outcomes, confront trade-offs, decide, tell your story. It is a useful skeleton for any AI-assisted options paper.

facts.t: Cameroon legislates in English and French, and both must be legally equivalent.
facts.more: An AI translation can quietly shift a term of art. In bilingual systems, qualified drafters must check that both texts carry the same legal meaning.

facts.t: The option every serious options matrix includes.
facts.more: Doing nothing, or improving existing measures, is the baseline the other options must beat on effectiveness, cost, equity, feasibility, legality, acceptability and risk.

labs.title: Build an evidence-based options paper
labs.intro: Put the analyst's steps in a sound order.
steps: Write a precise problem statement: who, how much, where, why
Trace each statistic to a national institute, admin data or peer-reviewed source
Research approaches used elsewhere and check them in primary sources
Assess whether each foreign approach transfers to your institutions and resources
Build an options matrix, including the status quo, against explicit criteria
Ask for the strongest case for and against each option
Consult affected groups and validate with legal and economic experts
labs.tip: Problem, then evidence, then comparison, then transferability, then options, then challenge, then consultation. AI helps at each step but owns none of them.

labs.title: Spot the problems in this AI policy brief
labs.intro: An AI drafted this brief on youth unemployment for a ministry in Yaoundé. Tap every passage that must not go to the minister unchecked.
segments: Youth unemployment and underemployment are a major concern in Cameroon's urban centres.
According to a 2023 World Bank study, exactly 61.4% of Douala graduates are jobless,
A precise figure with a vague citation is a classic fabrication pattern. Trace it to the actual report or remove it.
so the evidence base needs strengthening before options are finalised.
Rwanda's apprenticeship levy proves the model will work here,
It assumes transferability without assessing institutions, capacity and context, and 'proves' overclaims.
and there is no credible argument against it.
Balanced analysis requires the strongest counter-arguments. Leaving them out is a bias red flag.
Options considered include the status quo, a wage subsidy and a training voucher.
Each is assessed against cost, equity and feasibility.
The French version can be produced automatically and published the same day.
Both official-language versions must be legally equivalent and checked by qualified drafters.
Stakeholder consultation is recommended before a decision.
labs.tip: Check precise numbers, claims of proof, missing counter-arguments and bilingual equivalence.

modules.d: Clear, accessible, truthful communication and casework with citizens — with transparency about AI.
modules.body:
Communication is a public service

Citizens need clear, accurate information to access services, understand decisions and participate in public life. Elected representatives receive large volumes of constituent enquiries; government agencies must explain complex policies to diverse audiences. AI can help draft, simplify, translate and organise communication — making public communication faster and more accessible — provided accuracy, honesty and privacy are protected.

Plain language and accessibility

Plain language means people can find what they need, understand it and act on it the first time they read it. AI can rewrite official text at an accessible reading level, structure information with headings and steps, and create versions for different audiences — while experts check that meaning has not changed. Accessibility also includes formats for people with disabilities (screen-reader-friendly documents, captions, audio, sign language where possible) and materials in the languages people actually speak. In multilingual countries such as Cameroon — with English, French and many national languages — translation quality must be checked by fluent speakers.

Truthfulness standard. Public communication must not mislead. AI can make messages more persuasive and polished, but persuasion must rest on accurate facts. Never use AI to fabricate statistics, quotes, endorsements or images presented as real. Corrections should be prompt and visible when errors occur.

Casework and constituent services

Representatives and their staff handle requests about benefits, documents, local services and grievances. AI can help categorise incoming messages, draft acknowledgements, summarise cases, and produce first drafts of responses or letters to agencies. Safeguards: constituent data is personal and often sensitive — use approved tools with appropriate data protection; staff review every response; and complex or urgent cases (safety, health, legal deadlines) are prioritised for human attention.

Government chatbots and digital assistants

Public-service chatbots can answer common questions at any hour. Good practice: tell users they are interacting with an automated system; ground answers in current, authoritative official information; state limitations clearly; provide easy routes to human help; avoid collecting unnecessary personal data; log and review answers for accuracy; and update content when laws or procedures change. A chatbot that confidently gives wrong legal or benefits information can harm citizens and expose the institution to liability.

Crisis communication

During emergencies — floods, disease outbreaks, security incidents — speed matters, but accuracy matters more. AI can help draft templates in advance, translate updates quickly and summarise incoming public questions. Messages should be verified, consistent across channels, coordinated with responsible authorities and tested for clarity.

Listening at scale

AI can analyse large volumes of public feedback — consultation responses, social media comments, call-centre logs — to identify themes and emerging concerns. Treat such analysis with care: online voices may not represent the whole population, and analysis must respect privacy and avoid profiling individuals for their political opinions.

🧪 Interactive Lab — try it now

Act as my public communication assistant. I will paste an official notice or policy text. Rewrite it in plain language for the general public, keeping the meaning identical and listing any points where simplification might change meaning. Produce versions for social media and SMS, and flag what must be translated and checked by fluent speakers. Then draft a short FAQ answering the five questions citizens are most likely to ask.

📚 Glossary

  • Plain language: communication people understand and can act on the first time
  • Casework: handling individual constituents' requests and problems
  • Grounding: basing chatbot answers on authoritative sources
  • Profiling: automated evaluation of personal characteristics, including political opinions

📖 References

  • OECD — Good practice principles for public communication responses to mis- and disinformation.
  • PLAIN (Plain Language Association International) and plainlanguage.gov guidelines.
  • W3C — Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2.
  • UK Government Digital Service — content design guidance.

quiz.q: A Cameroonian municipal office uses AI to rewrite a birth-registration notice in plain French and English. What check is most important before publishing?
opts: Have experts confirm meaning is unchanged and fluent speakers check each language
Test the notice with two staff members who did not write the original text
Ask the AI to back-translate each version and compare the result with the original notice
Run the text through a readability score and aim for a primary-school level
quiz.x: The module requires experts to confirm meaning and fluent speakers to check translations. Back-translation is a useful runner-up but can miss legal nuances and register.

quiz.q: A US county launches a benefits chatbot. After a law change, it keeps citing the old income threshold for three weeks. Which practice would most likely have prevented this?
opts: Routing every question to a human, so the chatbot just greets users
Training the chatbot on a larger set of past citizen questions and answers
Grounding answers in current official content and updating it when rules change
Adding a disclaimer that answers may be inaccurate and are not legal advice
quiz.x: Grounding in current authoritative information and updating content when laws change addresses the root cause. A disclaimer is good practice but does not stop wrong figures harming citizens.

quiz.q: A member of parliament's office receives 400 messages a week. Staff want AI to categorise them and draft replies. One message mentions a constituent's eviction hearing in two days. What should the workflow do?
opts: Send an automated acknowledgement and ask the constituent to call the office
Flag urgent legal, health or safety cases for immediate human attention
Draft a reply automatically and queue it for review in the normal weekly batch
Forward the message to the court registry so the hearing can be postponed
quiz.x: Safeguards include prioritising complex or urgent cases such as legal deadlines for human attention. An acknowledgement is polite but leaves an urgent deadline in a queue.

quiz.q: A ministry spokesperson wants an AI-drafted press release to quote a local farmer praising a new subsidy, though no farmer has said this yet. What is the right course?
opts: Use the quote but attribute it to 'a farmer' without a name to avoid misleading
Publish it as illustrative and correct later if a farmer disagrees publicly
Ask the AI to generate a more modest quote that is less likely to be challenged
Do not publish an invented quote; gather a real, consented testimony instead
quiz.x: Fabricated quotes presented as real breach the truthfulness standard regardless of attribution. A modest invented quote is still invented.

quiz.q: A Nigerian state emergency agency is preparing for the flood season. How can AI help most responsibly before any flood occurs?
opts: Predict which households are likely to refuse evacuation, to target them with extra warnings
Draft verified message templates and translations in advance with the authorities
Generate live alerts automatically from social media reports of rising water
Write a single national message so every channel uses identical wording
quiz.x: Preparing templates and translations in advance, coordinated with responsible authorities, uses AI's speed while protecting accuracy. Auto-alerts from social media risk spreading unverified information.

quiz.q: A ministry analyses 50,000 social-media comments about a tax reform with AI and finds 70% are negative. The minister wants to cite this as public opinion. What is the main caution?
opts: The ministry needs consent from every commenter before analysing their posts
The AI sentiment model may have misclassified sarcasm in a small share of posts
Online voices may not represent the population, so it is not a measure of opinion
The figure should be rounded to 'most', since exact percentages invite challenge
quiz.x: Listening-at-scale analysis must be treated with care because online voices may not represent the whole population. Misclassification is real but smaller than the representativeness problem.

quiz.q: A US federal agency is redesigning its passport-renewal page. Under accessibility guidance such as WCAG, which change most improves access?
opts: Using headings, alt text and captions so screen readers and others can use it
Converting the instructions into a downloadable scanned PDF for printing
Shortening the page by moving all eligibility rules to a separate FAQ
Adding an AI avatar that reads the instructions aloud in a single language
quiz.x: Screen-reader-friendly structure, alternative text and captions are core accessibility measures. A scanned PDF is often unreadable by screen readers, and a single-language avatar helps only some users.

quiz.q: A constituency office wants to paste casework emails, including medical details, into a free consumer AI app to draft replies faster. What is the best advice?
opts: Stop using AI for casework and return to drafting each reply by hand
Allowed if the constituent's name is replaced with initials in each email
Allowed if staff delete the chat history after each session ends
Use an approved tool with data protection, and have staff review replies
quiz.x: Constituent data is personal and often sensitive, so approved tools with data protection plus staff review are required. Initials alone rarely anonymise medical details; deleting history does not control provider-side use.

quiz.q: A health ministry's chatbot tells a user it 'is a nurse named Grace'. What principle is violated, and what is the fix?
opts: Accessibility; give the bot a gender-neutral name and a simpler tone
Privacy; stop the bot asking for the user's name during the chat
Transparency; tell users they are talking to an automated system
Truthfulness; add a disclaimer at the end of each medical answer
quiz.x: Good practice requires telling users they are interacting with an automated system. A disclaimer about medical answers is useful but does not fix the misrepresentation of who the user is talking to.

quiz.q: A ministry discovers its AI-translated vaccination notice in Fulfulde gave the wrong clinic days. Thousands have seen it. What is the best response?
opts: Quietly replace the notice online so the error is no longer visible
Wait for the next scheduled bulletin to avoid confusing people further
Post the correction in French, the language most officials will read
Issue a prompt, visible correction in the same channels and language
quiz.x: Corrections should be prompt and visible, and in the channels and languages where people received the error. A silent replacement leaves those who saw the wrong days uninformed.

facts.t: Minimum WCAG text contrast ratio for normal-size text (level AA).
facts.more: Public notices and service portals that fail contrast exclude readers with low vision. WCAG 2.2 is the accessibility reference this module cites.

facts.t: Approximate number of languages spoken in Cameroon.
facts.more: Cameroon is among Africa's most linguistically diverse countries. Messages in English or French alone miss many citizens, and AI translation into national languages must be checked by fluent speakers.

facts.t: Year the US Plain Writing Act required federal agencies to use plain language.
facts.more: It shows plain language treated as a legal duty of public service, not just a style choice. plainlanguage.gov publishes the federal guidelines.

facts.t: The plain-language test: people find, understand and act on it the first time.
facts.more: Reading level is only one part of it. Structure, headings, steps and the right channel matter as much. Experts must confirm a simplified text still means the same thing.

labs.title: Government chatbot: good practice or red flag?
labs.intro: A city council plans a citizen-services chatbot. Sort each design choice.
items: Opening line says it is an automated assistant
Answers grounded in the current official fee schedule
'Talk to an officer' button on every screen
Asks for national ID number before answering general questions
Gives definitive answers on eligibility for benefits it can't verify
Chat logs reviewed weekly for wrong answers
Content last updated when the service launched two years ago
Uses a staff member's name and photo as the bot's persona
labs.tip: Disclose, ground, limit, hand over to humans, minimise data, review, and update.

labs.title: Spot the problems in this flood alert
labs.intro: An AI drafted this SMS-and-WhatsApp alert for a Douala sub-division. Tap every phrase that must be fixed before it goes out.
segments: FLOOD ALERT – Douala IV.
Heavy rain expected tonight.
Residents near the Mungo bridge should move to higher ground before 20:00.
The Governor has confirmed that all evacuees will receive 50,000 FCFA.
An unverified commitment attributed to an official. A fabricated promise like this damages trust and creates liability.
Shelter: Bonassama Government School.
Experts say this will be the worst flood in Cameroon's history.
An unsourced, alarmist claim. Crisis messages must be verified and must not exaggerate.
Families of Mr. Ekane, the drowned fisherman, should call 6XX XX XX XX.
It names a victim and adds a personal contact without consent. That is a privacy and dignity breach.
Emergency line: 117.
Message in English only to save time.
Crisis messages must reach people in the languages they speak, with translations checked by fluent speakers.
labs.tip: In a crisis, accuracy, coordination, privacy and language reach matter more than speed.

plaibox.title: Plain-language rewrite builder
plaibox.intro: Turn an official notice into a plain-language version for citizens. Copy the prompt, run it, then have a subject expert compare meanings.

fields.ph: e.g. Decree on new procedures for birth certificate registration...

fields.label: Who must understand it
fields.ph: e.g. rural parents, many with primary-level reading, mostly French-speaking

fields.label: What they must be able to do afterwards
fields.ph: e.g. register a birth within the legal deadline and know which documents to bring

fields.label: Channels and formats

fields.label: Languages needed
